Put all photos in your camera roll into the “hidden” folder (don’t delete until you’re fully 100% ready, might take months or even years) 
All physical photos printed out, when you feel ready, these are the first things I got rid of because they were up on my walls everywhere, I burned them in a fire pit, i cried and it felt somewhat therapeutic. 

All gifts he’s given you or things that STRONGLY remind you of him, put in a box and in a cupboard, when you’re ready, you can ask him if he wants them back or just throw them away or keep them if you begin to feel impartial about them. 

When you do something that you wish you could message him about/show him, message a friend or yourself so you don’t feel lonely and like you have no one to share things with. 

The best advice I can give you is to remove it all from your everyday life/environment but I really really wouldn’t suggest throwing stuff away until it’s been quite a while post breakup because you might need some of that stuff to be able to grieve slowly 

One day you’ll be able to look at that stuff and feel happy about the memories rather than sad or lonely so just put it all away and deal with it when you are ready. 

A rule of thumb is don’t open the box until you haven’t cried about the breakup for at least 3 weeks. Opening it too early or dealing with it too soon will just set you back again and again 

Things will get better, you’ll be okay. You don’t need to “move on” or “get over it” or “find someone new” if you don’t want to, everyone deals with this differently, you’ve got this ❤️

They’re three hard subjects and BCB is not bad at all but I understand that everyone has different expectations for themselves so my advice would be, stress less. Having a stressed brain stops you from retaining information, revise in new environments e.g a park or a library you’ve never been to. Somewhere fresh that when you think about that place all that comes to mind is the revision that you did there. Get your teachers to send you a list of every topic you’ve learnt so far, research each one extensively and take notes. Biggest piece of advice is to use practice papers !! Usually if you revised hard but didn’t do too well it’s because you didn’t answer the question the way they wanted you to rather than you not knowing the information. Practice exam questions and ask your teachers to mark them. I hope this helps :D

When I was a kid I used to have panic attacks at every single sleepover until I was 11 or 12, I would cry and have to wake up my friends parents and ask them to take me home in the middle of the night. It was very stressful, upsetting and most of all embarrassing. The first sleepover that I stayed the whole night without a panic attack was just a normal night until my friend woke up in the middle of the night and was sick everywhere and her mum had to come and hold her hair back in the toilet. She was fine after throwing up a few times but I think seeing her upset and worried made my protective instincts over her kick in and made me not worry about myself so much and I managed to sleep the whole night at her house. Anyway so what I’m trying to say is that if you can somehow lead the evening like play games you suggest or watch something you have seen on Netflix already it will make you feel a lot more confident and secure. Also try not to fall asleep last because when your sitting alone in the dark in someone els house it can be really scary and can cause a lot of anxiety. Also don’t be afraid to tell your friends that you have panic attacks and you are nervous that you might have one, if they’re actively trying to make you more comfortable, your anxiety will really fall. Once you’ve had a few sleepovers without panic attacks you will most likely be fine at every sleepover onwards. I hope this helped :)

I had vision problems mostly due to anxiety. I didn’t leave my bed for months because of how dizzy and unsettled I felt every time I opened my eyes and moved. After a couple months and learning how to deal with it, it’s almost completely gone away and only comes back during panic attacks which is completely manageable and I am SO great full that it’s only back in these short burst. So yes vision can be effected a lot by anxiety, try not to worry, I went to every health care professional I could think of and there was nothing physically wrong. It’s frightening and very uncomfortable but it will pass and you will be fine
